extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers reading/solving commutative algebra exercises (readers of Bourbaki / Math.StackExchange users)
extracted.subtask_description: Annotated solutions and comments for Chapter 3 (localization, flatness, tensor products, snake lemma, and related exercises) following Bourbaki; collects statements, equivalences, proofs and counterexamples useful when proving or checking results in commutative algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category of A-algebras has all limits and colimits
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a ring, the category of A-algebras has all limits and all colimits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To establish this it suffices to show existence of products, equalizers, coproducts and coequalizers. Products and equalizers can be computed in Sets; arbitrary coproducts are given by tensor products; the coequalizer of f,g: B ⇒ C is the canonical projection C → C/c where c is the ideal generated by elements f(b)-g(b). (Details are left to the reader.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness ⇔ vanishing Tor
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module M the following are equivalent: (i) M is flat; (ii) Tor^A_n(M,N)=0 for all n>0 and all A-modules N; (iii) Tor^A_1(M,N)=0 for all A-modules N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: (i)⇒(ii) by tensoring a free resolution of N with flat M; (iii)⇒(i) via the Tor long exact sequence applied to short exact sequences and showing M⊗– preserves injections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness in short exact sequence when quotient flat (Prop/Ex 2.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let 0→N'→N→N''→0 be exact with N'' flat. Then N' is flat iff N is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A long proof is provided that avoids Tor, following Bourbaki: uses the Snake Lemma and tensor diagrams. The shorter Tor-based proof (using Tor properties) is noted as simpler if Tor is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Snake Lemma (constructive formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commutative diagram of R-modules with exact rows and with u' injective and v surjective, there is a unique R-linear connecting map δ: Ker(γ) → Coker(α) characterized by a lifting property, and an exact long sequence Ker(α)→Ker(β)→Ker(γ)→Coker(α)→Coker(β)→Coker(γ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an explicit formula δ := p ◦ u'^{-1} ◦ β ◦ v^{-1} ◦ k and a detailed proof verifying well-definedness, linearity and exactness at each term; also displays the 'snake' diagram. Lemmas about images and kernels (20–23) are used in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring an exact sequence with a flat module preserves exactness (Lemma 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is flat and 0→M1→M2→M→0 is exact, then for any module N the sequence 0→M1⊗_R N → M2⊗_R N → M⊗_R N → 0 is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a short exact sequence 0→P→F→N→0 with F free, forms a commutative diagram of tensor products and applies the Snake Lemma; injectivity of certain maps follows from flatness of M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness equivalence in three-term exact sequence (Lemma 26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let 0→M'→M→M''→0 be exact with M'' flat. Then M' is flat iff M is flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs tensor diagrams with an arbitrary monomorphism N'→N and uses exactness from M'' flatness and Snake-Lemma-like kernel/image arguments to show equivalence of injectivity properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: M flat ⇔ injectivity on finitely generated ideals (Theorem 27 / Ex 2.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-module M is flat iff for every finitely generated ideal a of A the natural map M⊗_A a → M (sending x⊗a to xa) is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof (sketch following Bourbaki) introduces the notion 'M is N-flat' (injectivity for submodules of N) and shows that injectivity on finitely generated submodules suffices, then uses closure properties (submodules, quotients, direct sums) to deduce full flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: M is N-flat
rubrics_metrics.description: M is N-flat if for every submodule N'⊂N the natural map M⊗_A N' → M⊗_A N is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion is used to reduce flatness checks to finitely generated submodules and to prove properties like inheritance by submodules/quotients and behavior under direct sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction properties for N-flatness (parts (a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If M⊗N'→M⊗N is injective for every finitely generated submodule N' of N then M is N-flat. (b) If M is N-flat then M is P-flat for any submodule or quotient P of N. (c) If N = ⊕_{i∈I} N_i and M is N_i-flat for each i then M is N-flat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use finite-generation arguments, exact sequences with natural projections/inclusions, and induction on finite direct sums; the arbitrary direct-sum case is handled by considering finitely generated submodules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bourbaki finite condition for flatness (elementwise criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: M is N-flat iff for all finite families (x_i)⊂M, (y_i)⊂N with Σ x_i⊗y_i = 0 there exist finite families (a_{ij})⊂A and (x'_j)⊂M with x_i = Σ_j x'_j a_{ij} for all i and Σ_i a_{ij} y_i = 0 for all j. Specializing to N=A gives: M flat iff for every finite (x_i)⊂M and (a_i)⊂A with Σ x_i a_i = 0 there exist relations expressing x_i in terms of a finite set whose A-relations annihilate the a_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as Bourbaki's condition and follows from the tensor characterization; references and a proof sketch point to §3.1.3 and earlier reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of absolutely flat rings (Exercise 2.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A the following are equivalent: (i) A is absolutely flat (every A-module is flat); (ii) every principal ideal is idempotent; (iii) every finitely generated ideal is a direct summand of A. Also equivalent are: (iv) every finitely generated ideal generated by an idempotent; (v) for all a∈A there exists x with a=a^2 x; (vi) every ideal is idempotent; (vii) each principal ideal is radical; (viii) each ideal is radical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof directions given: (i)⇒(ii) by tensoring with A/(x); (ii)⇒(iii) constructs idempotents generating ideals; (iii)⇒(i) uses the criterion of Theorem 27. Notes: absolutely flat rings have no nonzero nilpotents and several logical equivalences among listed properties are explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal property and uniqueness of localization (Corollary 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If g:A→B is a ring homomorphism such that (i) g(s) is a unit in B for all s∈S; (ii) g(a)=0 implies as=0 for some s∈S; (iii) every element of B is of form g(a)g(s)^{-1}, then there is a unique isomorphism h:S^{-1}A→B with g = h◦f (f the canonical map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wording improved to assert uniqueness up to unique isomorphism; the third condition ensures surjectivity and the second ensures kernel corresponds to elements killed after localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of modules: S^{-1}M ≅ S^{-1}A ⊗_A M (Prop 3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a unique isomorphism f: S^{-1}A ⊗_A M → S^{-1}M with f((a/s)⊗m)=am/s for all a,m,s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The universal property of localization is stated: for any A-linear g:M→N into an S^{-1}A-module N that kills elements annihilated by some s∈S there is a unique S^{-1}A-linear h:S^{-1}M→N with g=h◦f. Also: if 1⊗x=0 in S^{-1}A⊗_A M then sx=0 for some s∈S (proof given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization distributes over tensor product (Prop 3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For A-modules M,N there is a unique isomorphism of S^{-1}A-modules f: S^{-1}M ⊗_{S^{-1}A} S^{-1}N → S^{-1}(M⊗_A N) with f((m/s)⊗(n/t))=(m⊗n)/st. In particular Mp⊗_{A_p} Np ≅ (M⊗_A N)_p for any prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives compatibility of localization with tensor products and is used in checking exactness and detecting non-vanishing after localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module is zero iff all localizations at primes/maximals zero (Prop 3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module M: M=0 ⇔ M_p=0 for all prime ideals p ⇔ M_m=0 for all maximal ideals m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary: an element a∈A is zero iff a/1 = 0 in every localization Ap (or in every Am). The result is used repeatedly to reduce global questions to local ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness can be checked after localization at maximal ideals (Prop 3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complex M→N→P of A-modules is exact iff for every maximal ideal m the localized complex M_m→N_m→P_m is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the identity Ker(g_m)/Im(f_m) ≅ (Ker(g)/Im(f))_m and Proposition 3.8 to reduce vanishing of homology to vanishing of its localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of ideals under localization (Prop 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For multiplicative S⊂A and ideal a⊂A: (i) every ideal in S^{-1}A is extended from A; (ii) (S^{-1}a)^c = ⋂_{s∈S} (a:s); in particular ae=(1) iff a meets S; (iii) a∈C ⇔ no element of S is a zero-divisor in A/a; (iv) prime ideals of S^{-1}A correspond bijectively to prime ideals of A disjoint from S via extension/contraction; (v) S^{-1} commutes with finite sums, products, intersections and radicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed derivation for part (ii) is given via element chasing. For (iv) contraction/extension give inverse inclusion-preserving bijections between Spec(S^{-1}A) and the set of primes of A not meeting S. A counterexample shows some naive converses can fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annihilator under localization: inclusion may be strict (Prop 3.14 comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an A-module M, S^{-1}Ann_A(M) ⊂ Ann_{S^{-1}A}(S^{-1}M) always holds, but the reverse inclusion need not hold in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counterexample: A=K[x], S=K[x]\\{0}, M=⊕_n A/(x^n) has Ann M = (0) but S^{-1}M = 0 so Ann S^{-1}M = (1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction criterion for primes under a ring map (Prop 3.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let f:A→B and p a prime ideal of A. Then p is the contraction of a prime ideal of B iff p^e_c = p (i.e., extension then contraction gives back p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use localization diagrams and consider the induced maps on localizations; compare with related exercises (3.21iv). A strengthening describes the set Σ of ideals of B contracting to a fixed a⊂A and shows minimal/maximal/prime properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor criterion for contraction of primes (related result / eq. (18))
rubrics_metrics.description: p is the contraction of a prime ideal of B iff (A_p/p_p) ⊗_A B ≠ 0 (equivalently Ap/pp ⊗_A B ≠ 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim decomposes several canonical B-algebras and shows canonical bijections; a short elementwise criterion for checking contraction/non-contraction is given in Claim 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: S^{-1}M = 0 for finitely generated M ⇔ some s∈S annihilates M (Ex 3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated, then S^{-1}M=0 iff ∃ s∈S such that sM = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: if S^{-1}M=0 and x_1,...,x_n generate M then for each i there exists s_i with s_i x_i = 0, so product annihilates M; conversely obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: S = 1 + a: S^{-1}a lies in the Jacobson radical (Ex 3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S = 1 + a (a an ideal) then S^{-1}a is contained in the Jacobson radical of S^{-1}A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the identity 1 - (α/(1+β))·(a/(1+γ)) = (1+β+γ+βγ-αa)/(1+β+γ+βγ) and show numerator ∈ S, hence units exist; apply Nakayama for module consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isomorphism (ST)^{-1}A ≅ U^{-1}(S^{-1}A) where U image of T (Ex 3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S,T are multiplicative subsets and U is the image of T in S^{-1}A, then (ST)^{-1}A and U^{-1}(S^{-1}A) are isomorphic as A-algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct mutual inverse A-algebra maps f,g by tracking images of a/(st) and verifying unit conditions; explicit formulas provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of S^{-1}B and f(S)^{-1}B for ring map f (Ex 3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:A→B and T=f(S), then S^{-1}B and T^{-1}B are isomorphic as S^{-1}A-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define a bijection via (b,s)↦(b,f(s)) on the standard quotient presentations B×S/~ and B×T/~; check equivalence relations coincide and linearity follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local nilpotents detection: if Ap have no nilpotents then A has none (Ex 3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: If for each prime p the local ring A_p has no nilpotent element (A_p ≠ 0), then A has no nilpotent elements. However, even if each A_p is a domain, A need not be a domain (e.g., product of two fields).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 3.8 (local detection) or the nilradical localization corollary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal multiplicative sets correspond to complements of minimal primes (Ex 3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set Σ of multiplicative subsets not containing 0 has maximal elements; S∈Σ is maximal iff A\S is a minimal prime ideal of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Zorn's Lemma (chains union in Σ) and localization nonvanishing to produce primes disjoint from S and deduce equality by maximality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saturated multiplicative subset characterization (Ex 3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: S is saturated (xy∈S ⇔ x∈S and y∈S) iff A\S is a union of prime ideals. The saturation of S is the complement of the union of primes disjoint from S and is the least saturated multiplicative subset containing S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved by contraposition using element as unit in S^{-1}A; special case S=1+a has saturation equal to complement of union of maximal ideals containing a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for S^{-1}A→T^{-1}A bijectivity (Ex 3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For S⊂T multiplicative, the canonical map φ:S^{-1}A→T^{-1}A is bijective iff for each t∈T, t/1 is a unit in S^{-1}A iff ∀ t∈T ∃ x∈A with x t ∈ S iff T is contained in the saturation of S iff every prime meeting T meets S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chain of equivalences provided with proofs: (i)⇒(ii) easy; (ii)⇒(iii) by expressing inverse; (v) relates primes and units via localization at primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-divisors are union of prime ideals; minimal primes consist of zero-divisors (Ex 3.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: The set of zero-divisors in A is a union of prime ideals. Any minimal prime ideal consists of zero-divisors. In localized rings an element that is neither unit nor zero-divisor leads to contradictions in certain situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two proofs referenced: one via Exercise 1.14 and another via the saturation/primality exercises; provides an argument showing minimal primes consist of zero-divisors using maximality of multiplicative subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves absolute flatness; characterization via local fields (Ex 3.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) If A is absolutely flat then S^{-1}A is absolutely flat for any S. (ii) A is absolutely flat iff A_m is a field for every maximal ideal m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses earlier equivalences for absolutely flat rings and localization properties; converses use checking mm=(0) locally and then global equivalences from Exercise 2.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological/algebraic equivalences for Spec(A) (Ex 3.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring A with nilradical N, the following are equivalent: (i) A/N is absolutely flat; (ii) every prime ideal of A is maximal; (iii) Spec(A) is a T1-space; (iv) Spec(A) is Hausdorff. If these hold, Spec(A) is compact and totally disconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implications (iv)⇒(iii)⇔(ii) trivial; (ii)⇒(iv) shown via existence of elements separating distinct primes (open sets Xa and Xb) using multiplicative sets avoiding 0; further details link local algebra mm=(0) to absolute flatness.
